html:
Iskandar Muda was the sultan of Aceh, in north Sumatra, from 1607 to 1636. Under him Aceh reached its height, ruling much of Sumatra and parts of the Malay peninsula.

He controlled the pepper trade and fought the Portuguese in Malacca, whom he besieged in 1629 with a great fleet, though he was defeated. His court drew Muslim scholars, and Aceh became known as the porch of Mecca, where pilgrims sailed for Arabia.

Aceh's strict Muslim identity and long independence led to the Aceh War with the Dutch and later to its special status under Indonesia, where it now applies Islamic law. See Islam and Pasai.
sum: Iskandar Muda was the sultan of Aceh, in north Sumatra, from 1607 to 1636. Under him Aceh reached its height, ruling much of Sumatra and parts of the Malay peninsula.
